A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-equivariance evaluations, downstream task experiments, finetuning ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds numerical results for the feature-layer fusion ablation.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains multiview correspondence finetuning using SmoothAP, LoRA and one additional convolutional layer. Specifying that LoRA operates in the last four blocks adds implementation detail without establishing a method revision.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained throughout, including the main correspondence tasks and appendix recognition, segmentation, depth and background-invariance evaluations. The added feature-fusion table uses existing benchmarks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including the evaluated backbones and DUSt3R, FiT/FiT-Reg, OnePose++, MegaPose and Co-Tracker in their respective comparisons. The fusion configurations tabulated in v2 were already described in v1.

E3.justification: No revision to an existing evaluation protocol is documented. Evaluation every tenth video frame is newly disclosed for OnePose-LowTexture; v1 states no conflicting sampling interval. The layer-fusion configurations and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.8.1 already describes feature-layer fusion and its qualitative findings in v1, but lacks the referenced results table. v2 adds Table 16 comparing the final layer with two fusion configurations across pose estimation, tracking and semantic correspondence, supplying quantitative support for this existing ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added Table 16 follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerical fusion results in Table 16. For example, layers 8,9,10,11 yield OnePose-LowTex 3cm-3deg accuracy of 60.35 and tracking AJ of 41.25, versus 58.03 and 46.85 for layer 11. These values were absent from v1; existing benchmark results and qualitative figures remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 retains the same APE, PCDP and SmoothAP definitions and mathematical explanation. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: evaluating multiview equivariance, relating it to downstream correspondence performance, and improving features through minimal finetuning, including one-object, one-iteration training.

C2.justification: Interpretations of layer specialization, synthetic-to-real transfer, convolutional overfitting and background invariance are retained, as are the qualifications about weaker benefits on other semantic tasks. Table 16 supports the existing interpretation in Appendix A.8.1.

D1.justification: v2 specifies LoRA placement in the last four blocks, every-tenth-frame OnePose-LowTexture evaluation, and layer 11 as the final feature layer. These disclosures improve reproducibility. The existing repository URL is relocated without changing access information.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning against prior 3D-awareness studies, FiT, DVT and DUSt3R are unchanged. Conference identification and citation styling do not alter the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a Statements section containing ethics and reproducibility statements, updates acknowledgements, shortens the abstract and clarifies several technical sentences. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 16, renumbers the background-invariance table to Table 17, relocates Table 2 and reformats Table 13 with a clearer PF-PASCAL viewpoint label. Conference headers, colored links and spacing change, while all existing figure images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves a specific evidentiary gap by supplying the missing feature-fusion results in Appendix A.8.1. The LoRA placement and frame-sampling disclosures also make reproduction easier. These are useful, limited gains in completeness and transparency; the central method, benchmark findings and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
